Subject: Realtime: sudden pacing surge causing 5-10s chunk delays

Hi Aditya,

We started seeing a sharp increase in latency on our live chat integrations around 07:05 UTC this morning. Streaming chunks are frequently delayed between 5–10s and some sessions are timing out. It affects ~12% of active sessions; error rates are low but perceived responsiveness is poor.

Attached is a short capture from our client showing token cadence (latency-sample-170117.txt). We rely on the streaming endpoint for interactive advisor flows and this is impacting callers.

Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing any degradation or routing changes in us-east-1? We need immediate mitigations while you triage.

Thanks,
Sonia
Sonia Patel

Subject: Re: Realtime: sudden pacing surge causing 5-10s chunk delays

Hi Sonia — thanks for the heads up and for the sample. We're on it. High level: we see an elevated request pacing pattern that is increasing downstream KV cache thrashing on a subset of streaming shards in us-east-1. Immediate steps we recommend you try (should reduce perceived latency within minutes):

1) Temporarily set streaming.chunk_size to 512 tokens (from default 1024) to shorten chunk generation windows.
2) Reduce max_response_tokens to 256 for interactive flows where safe.
3) If you have a fallback path, enable short-polling (poll interval 300–500ms) for critical sessions until we stabilize.
4) Add a soft client-side retry of 1 attempt with exponential backoff (250ms -> 600ms) rather than aggressive reconnects.

We have looped in Eng (karthik) to triage routing and cache warming. Can you please attach a 2-minute tracing capture (pacing-capture-170117.json) from 07:03–07:05 UTC and paste the example request_id from an affected session? That will give us the shard mapping quickly.

I'll provide an update in ~30m. Apologies for the disruption — we know this flow is high priority for FinBank.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Subject: Re: Realtime: sudden pacing surge causing 5-10s chunk delays

Update from Eng (summary):
- Root cause (initial): transient routing imbalance across three streaming shards in us-east-1 caused elevated KV cache misses and small head-of-line stalls for long-running sessions. A background autoscaling decision unusually redistributed hot sessions during an internal maintenance window.
- Action taken: engineering applied an immediate routing pin for FinBank's shard mapping, forced KV cache warmups for the affected shards, and reverted the maintenance reassignments.

Customer-facing mitigations we've applied (done):
- Routing pin + cache warmup (server-side) — should reduce new chunk latency within ~2–4 minutes.
- Temporary routing fallback enabled to alternate healthy shard pool if latency exceeds 1.5s per chunk (server-side).

What we ask you to do (recommended immediate):
1) Apply the streaming.chunk_size and max_response_tokens changes from my previous note (client-side) for the next 1–2 hours.
2) Keep short-poll fallback enabled only for critical sessions.

We'll monitor the dashboard and share a short incident brief within 24 hours. If you still see >2s chunk delays after 10m, please send those request_ids and timestamps and we'll escalate to on-call infra.

Apologies again — we're treating this as priority.

Regards,
Aditya

Hi Sonia — following up with a short post-incident summary and recommended durable actions. Thank you for the quick traces; they were invaluable.

Incident summary (brief):
- Window: 2027-01-17 07:03–07:27 UTC.
- Impact: elevated per-chunk latency (median increase from ~120ms to ~1.8s) affecting ~12% of active live-chat sessions in us-east-1. No replayed tokens or model correctness regressions observed.
- Root cause: ephemeral routing imbalance + KV cache cold starts triggered by an autoscaling reassign during an internal maintenance operation.

Permanent mitigations we will implement or recommend:
1) Pinning policy: we will allow a customer-requested soft pin for high-priority accounts to avoid maintenance-driven reassigns (target: Q1 2027 rollout).
2) Cache warmup heuristic: proactive KV warmups for long-lived sessions during scaling events (in flight).
3) Improved autoscaler safety: add a safety window that avoids moving hot shards during maintenance.
4) Client best practices (recommended): default streaming.chunk_size 512 for high-interactivity flows; add client-side jittered backoff for reconnects; expose a per-session health hook that falls back to polling after two consecutive >2s chunks.

Compensation & follow-up:
- We will apply a service credit equivalent to one day of stream usage for FinBank under DB-4987. Our CS team (marissa) will follow up with the credit note and formal incident doc.
- Engineering will share a public-facing postmortem draft for your review in 72 hours.

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough of the incident timeline with Eng and Product this week. Proposed times: Jan 19, 09:00 or 16:00 ET.

Thanks again for working through this quickly. Let me know if you want the immediate mitigations auto-applied to your account while we push the longer-term soft-pin feature.

Best,
